notes: What a party can gather for a day in a settlement's domain (Plan 5a, design §10b): one rule per good and kind of land. The lead rolls the skill against the DC, lowered by 1 per output level where the domain makes the good (GATHER_DC_PER_OUTPUT), and the whole able party works: `yield` is the units per tier for two workers, scaled by the workers and lowered as the land is picked over (GATHER_DEPTH_DAYS). Yields are set so a fresh day's work for two sells for about 3–6 gp in the domain, before depletion and bulk pressure: food and fuel sell at the 1 gp floor, timber and stone are heavy, healing herbs are the hardest and most valuable. Every land biome has at least one rule (a content test checks this). Written by Claude; tuned by the I1 economy report.

entries.label: Cut timber
entries.text: Fell and trim what the woodsmen left standing, and drag it to the road.

entries.label: Quarry stone
entries.text: Break good stone out of an old cutting and lever it onto a sledge.

entries.label: Gather firewood
entries.text: Deadfall, windblown branches and the odd stump, bundled for the town's hearths.

entries.label: Cut peat
entries.text: Slice turves from the bog and stack them to drain.

entries.label: Gather scrub and dung
entries.text: Thornwood roots and dried dung: what burns where nothing grows.

entries.label: Hunt and snare game
entries.text: Set snares at dawn, stalk at dusk, and smoke what you catch.

entries.label: Fish and forage
entries.text: Weirs in the shallows, roots and fruit along the banks.

entries.label: Gather healing herbs
entries.text: Woundwort, feverfew and moss, found by those who know the leaf, and dried for kits.
